strengths.I004: Changes the content of the finalists using an independent adversary's stated loss reasons, which a lone agent cannot obtain. Length is capped at +/-5% and a different-family verifier must prefer the revision in both orders, so the loop only moves in the verifier's favour and verbosity and position effects are controlled.
strengths.I003: Very cheap, since it changes only the scoring module and adds one labelling call. It can be tested offline by replaying saved pairwise records. It targets a real flaw in top-k selection: correlated duplicates reduce best-of-3 value.

verdicts.reason: I004 improves the substance of the delivered ideas through independent loss-conditioned revision. I003 only reorders an existing finalist set, so its gain disappears if finalists are already diverse, and it can lower mean-of-3 by construction.

strengths.I005: Takes persuasive critic prose away from the selector and ranks ideas on sandbox-executed or library-grounded checks. This gives an outcome-style signal (falsified-claim rate) that is harder for eloquence to game, with a clean prose/ledger switch.
strengths.I006: Turns executed checks into a cross-run template library. That advantage compounds over runs, and a single agent cannot match it. The loop is bounded to 3 iterations and has a separate flag that isolates the library from the loop.

verdicts.reason: I006 depends on I005's ledger already existing, roughly doubles development tokens and has 7 open major critiques. I005 is the self-contained foundation, buildable in about a week at +30-50% critique tokens.

strengths.I004: A standalone development sub-phase with explicit bias controls (length budget, both-order acceptance, a third-family verifier) and a three-arm design that isolates the value of the loss reasons.
strengths.I006: Scores development on re-executed checks rather than opinion, and it builds reusable check templates across runs.

verdicts.reason: I004 can be built in about a week at about +25% run cost without prerequisites. I006 needs a claim-ledger infrastructure that does not yet exist, costs about 2x development tokens and carries many unresolved major critiques, including developers weakening claims to trivial ones.

strengths.I004: Directly improves finalist content using independent judges' loss reasons, with length-matched, both-order-verified acceptance.
strengths.I008: Calibrates each judge's discrimination, position bias and self-preference against external rater verdicts. It then spends the same comparison budget on reliable judges near the top-3 boundary, at zero extra tokens. It can be validated offline against external rankings using Kendall tau.

verdicts.reason: I008 explicitly models and subtracts position and same-family bias, anchored to external verdicts. I004's acceptance gate still rests on one LLM judge's preference, so its gains may reflect that judge's style.
